units.title: Personal aspects of the Prophet's life
points: Ancestry and the main events of his early years, from birth to parenthood.
Early influences, including his parents, Abu Talib and Bahira.
His work and business before the revelation of the Qur'an.
His relationships with his wives and children.
Why his early life mattered for his later work as Allah's messenger.

units.title: The Revelation of the Qur'an
keyTerms: Laylat al-Qadr (لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْر), the Night of Power
points: The events of the Night of Power (Night of Decree).
Details of the conversation with Jibrail in the cave at Hira.
Why this experience mattered in the establishment of Islam.
The importance of the revelation of the Qur'an to Muslims.
How the Qur'an was compiled.

units.title: The Prophethood of Muhammad
keyTerms: Khatam an-Nabiyyin (خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّين), Seal of the Prophets
points: The meaning of the title 'Seal of the Prophets'.
The importance of Muhammad's role as prophet in establishing Islam.
The opposition faced in Makkah by the Prophet and his followers.

units.title: Opposition and Hijrah
points: The events of the boycott and the Mi'raj.
The plot to kill the Prophet and the details of the flight to Madinah.
The welcome by the people of Madinah and the building of mosques there.
The significance of the Hijrah for the Prophet and the early community.
Support given to the Prophet by Abu Bakr, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Uthman and Umar.
The contribution of the Companions and the helpers (Ansar) to establishing Islam.

units.title: The Sunnah of the Prophet
points: The importance for Muslims of his teachings, deeds and sayings.
How the Sunnah was recorded.
The role of the Sunnah in establishing Islamic belief and practice.

units.title: Teachings and example of the Prophet on justice and equality
points: His teaching and example on social and economic justice.
His teaching and example on human rights.
His relationship with people of other religions.
His teaching on respect for mothers and for women.
What these teachings show about Muslim beliefs about society.

units.title: The Prophet as leader
points: His role in the establishment of the Shari'ah.
The consolidation and expansion of Islam after the Hijrah.
His treatment of opponents and prisoners.
His relationship with other communities and countries.

units.title: Battles fought by the Prophet
points: The battles fought after the Hijrah: Badr, Ohud, the Trench and Khyber.
The reasons the Prophet chose to fight each battle.
The importance of the battles for the establishment of Islam.

units.title: The Prophet's final acts and his achievements
keyTerms: Hajjat al-Wada' (حَجَّةُ الوَدَاع), the Farewell Pilgrimage
points: His final pilgrimage and sermon.
The main themes and importance of his example and teaching in his later years.
His significant achievements in society, religion and politics.
The events at his death in Madinah.

units.title: The nature of belief in Allah
points: The meaning and importance of belief in the oneness of Allah (Tawhid).
The attributes of Allah: omnipotence, creator, merciful and just.
The meaning and importance of teaching about shirk and nifaq (hypocrisy).
The characteristics of Allah as shown in the Qur'an.

units.title: Risalah
points: The nature and importance of prophethood for Muslims.
What the roles of prophets teach Muslims.
The lives of earlier prophets: Adam, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Musa, Dawud and Isa.

units.title: The holy books of Islam
points: The nature of the Tawrat, Zabur, Injil and the Scrolls of Abraham.
The importance of these holy books in the establishment of Islam.

units.title: al-Qadr
points: The nature and importance of predestination for Muslims.
How al-Qadr and free will relate to the Day of Judgment.
The significance of belief in al-Qadr for the early Islamic community.
The nature and significance of evil and suffering.

units.title: Akhirah
points: Teachings about life after death: the final judgment.
Paradise (Jannah) and hell (Jahannam).
Life in the grave and Barzakh.
How these teachings are expressed in the Qur'an.

units.title: Malaikah
points: The nature and importance of angels for Muslims.
The roles and importance of Jibrail, Mikail, Israfil and Izrael.

units.title: Shari'ah
points: The principal sources of Shari'ah law: the Qur'an and the Sunnah.
The importance of the Shari'ah in the early Islamic community.
Related sources of law: ijma (consensus) and qiyas (analogy).
The difference between halal and haram in Muslim acts.
The five categories: fard, mandub, mubah, makruh and haram.

units.title: Islamic etiquette, attitude and manners
points: Islamic etiquette in relations with other people.
Islamic attitudes to lying and harmful speech.
Islamic manners when eating.
Why correct etiquette matters, with support from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

units.title: The early leaders of the Muslim community
points: Leadership of Islam after the death of the Prophet.
The role and achievements of the early leaders.
The importance of the period of the early leaders for the Islamic community.

units.title: Shahadah
points: The nature and role of Shahadah for Muslims.
The importance of reciting the Shahadah.
How the Shahadah is used in practice.

units.title: Salah
points: The nature, significance and importance of Salah in Muslim life.
How Salah is performed: ablution, times, directions, movements and recitations.
Salah in the home, in the mosque and at Friday (Jummah) prayer.
Exemptions from Salah.

units.title: Sawm
points: The nature, role, significance and purpose of fasting in Ramadan.
Those who are exempt from fasting.
The importance of Laylat al-Qadr for Muslims today.

units.title: Zakah and Khums
points: The nature and purpose of Zakah.
The nature and purpose of Khums.
The importance of Zakah and Khums for Muslims.
The global importance of giving support to those in need.

units.title: Hajj
points: The nature, role, origins and significance of Hajj.
Key actions performed during Hajj.
The importance of Hajj for Muslims.
Benefits and challenges of attending Hajj.
Exemptions from performing Hajj.

units.title: Jihad
points: The origins, meaning and significance of jihad in Islam.
The distinction between the greater (inner) and lesser (outer) jihad.
The importance of the greater jihad in Muslim life.
Conditions for declaring lesser jihad, with reference to Surah 2:190-194 and 22:39.

units.title: Islamic festivals
points: The origins and activities of Eid-ul-Adha, Eid-ul-Fitr and Ashura.
The meaning and significance of the festivals for Muslims.

units.title: Marriage and the family
points: The significance of marriage in Islamic life.
Muslim teachings about marriage.
Muslim teachings about the purpose of families.
Ceremonies relating to birth and death, and their meaning.
The importance of procreation in strengthening the Ummah.

units.title: Muslim citizenship and religious and political leadership
points: Muslim beliefs about leadership and the responsibility of religious and political leaders.
The challenges faced by leaders of Islam in the modern world.
The challenges and responsibilities of citizenship for Muslims.
The Prophet and his successors as models of leadership.

mathematics.subject: Mathematics
mathematics.label: Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
mathematics.statusNote: Rebuilt on 9 November 2026 from the official Pearson 4MA1 specification PDF (Issue 2), read as raw text: papers, durations, marks, weights, tiers, calculator rules, assessment objective weightings and every Foundation and Higher content statement. Pupils sit 4MA1, so the course is now taught from 4MA1 itself (it was previously taught from the UK GCSE 1MA1 with a 4MA1 exam entry). Units are the 32 Higher units of Pearson's two-year 4MA1 scheme of work, the school's KS4 maths scheme (a generic Pearson document), placed in the scheme's suggested Higher order over five terms with the sixth for revision. Each point is paraphrased with its 4MA1 reference; Higher assumes the Foundation content, so Foundation references are included. Series: January and June.
mathematics.tiers: Foundation (Papers 1F and 2F, grades 5 to 1) or Higher (Papers 1H and 2H, grades 9 to 4, with grade 3 allowed). The school teaches the Higher tier; Higher questions assume Foundation content.
mathematics.nonExam: None. Two externally assessed written papers only.

assessment.title: Higher tier paper 1
assessment.content: All Higher content, assuming the Foundation content: number, algebra, sequences, functions and graphs, geometry, vectors, statistics and probability
assessment.format: Written paper set and marked by Pearson; calculator allowed; Higher formulae sheet supplied; about 40% of marks at grades 4 and 5.

assessment.title: Higher tier paper 2
assessment.content: All Higher content, assuming the Foundation content
assessment.format: Written paper set and marked by Pearson; calculator allowed; Higher formulae sheet supplied; instruments and tracing paper may be used.

aos.desc: Number and algebra: numbers, calculations, numerical problems, equations, formulae, identities, sequences, functions and graphs.
Shape, space and measures: geometry, trigonometry, vectors and transformation geometry.
Handling data: statistics and probability.

commandWords.meaning: Find a numerical answer, showing the method.
Give enough working to reach a stated answer convincingly.
Give a logical argument, with justified steps, that a result is always true (Higher).
State why, using mathematical language or a rule.
Find the value or values of the unknown that satisfy the equation.
Rewrite an expression in the required algebraic form.
Use rounded values to find an approximate answer.
Show the key features of a graph or shape, with accuracy as the question requires.

gaps: Command words are not defined in the specification; the list uses wording common in Pearson papers and should be checked against current mark schemes.
Pearson may publish a later issue; check the live 4MA1 page before each academic year.

Portal lessons written for 1MA1 that are not on 4MA1 are not taught: y10 20 (product rule), 41 (exponential graphs), 48 (geometric and Fibonacci-type sequences), 50 (quadratic nth term), 66 (loci), 74 (frustums), 77 (frequency trees); y11 15 (exponential graphs), 18 (equation of a circle), 20, 21 and 26 (iteration), 30 (proving circle theorems), 32 (plans and elevations), 44 and 51 (sampling), 47 (box plots), 49 (scatter graphs). TO CONFIRM: retire or rewrite them in the lesson stage.
TO CONFIRM: the 4MA1 textbook edition the school holds (resources name Pearson's scheme of work units and portal lessons only).

units.title: Decimals
points: Use decimal notation and place value; order and convert decimals (1.3).
Convert recurring decimals into fractions (1.3A, Higher).
Round to a given number of significant figures or decimal places (1.8B).
Use estimation to approximate and check calculations (1.8D).
Use a scientific calculator efficiently to find numerical results (1.11A).

units.title: Special numbers, powers and roots
points: Identify square, cube and prime numbers, factors and multiples (1.4).
Express integers as products of powers of prime factors (1.4D).
Find highest common factors and lowest common multiples (1.4E).
Understand surds; simplify them and rationalise a denominator (1.4A, 1.4B, Higher).
Use index laws with integer, fractional and negative powers in numerical expressions (1.4C, Higher).

units.title: Algebraic manipulation
points: Use index laws in simple algebraic cases (2.1D).
Use index notation with fractional, negative and zero powers (2.1A, Higher).
Collect like terms, expand a single bracket and take out common factors (2.2B to 2.2D).
Expand the product of two or more linear expressions (2.2A, Higher).
Factorise quadratic expressions, including ax² + bx + c and the difference of two squares (2.2B, Higher).
Manipulate algebraic fractions with numeric, linear or quadratic parts (2.2C, Higher).
Complete the square for a quadratic expression (2.2D, Higher).
Use algebra to support and construct proofs (2.2E, Higher).

units.title: Expressions, formulae and rearranging formulae
points: Substitute positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions into expressions and formulae (2.3C).
Turn formulae given in words or diagrams into letters and symbols (2.3D).
Derive a formula or expression (2.3E).
Change the subject, including where it appears twice or as a power (2.3A, Higher).
Set up direct and inverse proportion problems and link them to graphs (2.5A, Higher).

units.title: Linear equations and inequalities
points: Solve linear equations with integer or fractional coefficients, unknowns on one or both sides (2.4A).
Set up simple linear equations from given information (2.4B).
Solve simple linear inequalities and show the solution set on a number line (2.8C).

units.title: Sequences
points: Generate terms of a sequence from term-to-term and position-to-term rules (3.1).
Use the first term (a) and common difference (d) of an arithmetic sequence (3.1A, Higher).
Know and use nth term = a + (n − 1)d (3.1B, Higher).
Find the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series (3.1C, Higher).

units.title: Graphical representation of data
points: Present data with pictograms, bar charts, pie charts and two-way tables, and interpret them (6.1).
Construct and interpret histograms for continuous data with unequal class intervals (6.1A, Higher).
Construct cumulative frequency diagrams from tabulated data (6.1B, Higher).
Use cumulative frequency diagrams (6.1C, Higher).

units.title: Statistical measures
points: Understand the concept of average (6.2A).
Calculate the mean, median, mode and range for a discrete data set (6.2B).
Estimate the mean and identify the modal class for grouped data (6.2C, 6.2D).
Estimate the median from a cumulative frequency diagram (6.2A, Higher).
Understand spread; find the interquartile range from data and from a cumulative frequency diagram (6.2B to 6.2D, Higher).

units.title: Fractions
points: Order fractions and find a fraction of a quantity (1.2D).
Express one number as a fraction of another (1.2E).
Convert a fraction to a decimal or a percentage (1.2G).
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers using common denominators (1.2F).
Multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers; fractions as multiplicative inverses (1.2H, 1.2I).

units.title: Percentages
points: Express a number as a percentage of another; convert percentages to fractions and decimals (1.6B, 1.6C).
Use percentages as multipliers; solve percentage increase and decrease problems (1.6D, 1.6E).
Use reverse percentages (1.6F).
Use compound interest and depreciation (1.6G).
Use repeated percentage change and solve compound interest problems (1.6A, 1.6B, Higher).

units.title: Ratio and proportion
points: Use ratio notation, simplify ratios and link ratios to fractions (1.7A).
Divide a quantity in a given ratio or ratios (1.7B).
Use proportion to find unknown quantities, including direct proportion (1.7C, 1.7D).
Solve word problems about ratio and proportion (1.7E).
Use number in everyday life, with standard units, time and money, including currency conversion (1.10A to 1.10C).

units.title: Indices and standard form
points: Use index laws for multiplication and division of integer powers, including zero (1.4C).
Calculate with and interpret numbers in standard form (1.9A).
Solve problems involving standard form (1.9A, Higher).

units.title: Compound measures
points: Use compound measures such as speed, density and pressure (4.4G).
Convert metric measurements of length and area (4.9A).
Convert between metric units of volume (4.10A).

units.title: Geometry of shapes
points: Use angle properties of intersecting and parallel lines and angles on a straight line (4.1B).
Use the angle properties of isosceles, equilateral and right-angled triangles (4.1D).
Use the angle sum and properties of quadrilaterals, including parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium and kite (4.2B, 4.2C).
Calculate interior and exterior angles of polygons and regular polygons (4.2D, 4.2E).
Give reasons using standard geometrical statements for angles in lines, polygons and circles (4.7A, Higher).

units.title: Real-life graphs
points: Interpret information in linear and non-linear graphs, including distance-time and speed-time graphs (3.3A).
Read rates from real-life graphs, such as speed from a distance-time graph (3.3A).

units.title: Linear graphs
points: Find the midpoint of a line segment from its end points (3.3E).
Find the gradient of a straight line; recognise y = mx + c with gradient m and intercept c (3.3G, 3.3H).
Generate points and plot graphs of linear functions (3.3I).
Calculate the gradient from two points; find lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line (3.3F, 3.3G, Higher).
Show simple linear inequalities on graphs and identify regions, including harder examples (2.8D, 2.8E; 2.8B, Higher).

units.title: Quadratic equations, inequalities and graphs
points: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation (2.7A).
Solve quadratics with the quadratic formula or by completing the square (2.7B, Higher).
Form and solve quadratic equations from a context (2.7C, Higher).
Solve quadratic inequalities and show the solution set on a number line (2.8A, Higher).
Plot graphs of quadratic functions (3.3I).

units.title: Constructions and bearings
points: Construct triangles and other 2D shapes with ruler, protractor and compasses (4.5B).
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line and the bisector of an angle (4.5D).
Use three-figure bearings (4.4D).
Solve problems with scale drawings; use and interpret maps (4.5C, 4.11B).

units.title: Perimeter, area and volume
points: Find perimeters and areas of triangles, rectangles, parallelograms and trapezia (4.9B to 4.9D).
Find circumferences and areas of circles and semicircles (4.9E).
Find perimeters and areas of sectors of circles (4.9A, Higher).
Find surface areas of simple shapes and of a cylinder (4.10C, 4.10D).
Find volumes of prisms, including cuboids and cylinders (4.10E).
Find the surface area and volume of a sphere and a right circular cone (4.10A, Higher).

units.title: Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry
points: Know, understand and use Pythagoras' theorem in two dimensions (4.8A).
Use sine, cosine and tangent of acute angles to find lengths and angles (4.8B).
Apply trigonometry to problems in two dimensions (4.8C).
Use sine, cosine and tangent of obtuse angles (4.8A, Higher).
Use angles of elevation and depression (4.8B, Higher).

units.title: Transformations
points: Rotate a shape about a centre through a given angle; anticlockwise is positive (5.2A to 5.2C).
Reflect a shape in a mirror line and construct the mirror line (5.2D, 5.2E).
Translate a shape using a column vector (5.2F to 5.2H).
Know that rotations, reflections and translations give congruent images (5.2I).
Enlarge a shape from a centre by a scale factor; angles are preserved, lengths are not (5.2J to 5.2L).
Give complete descriptions of transformations (5.2M).

units.title: Harder graphs and transformation of graphs
points: Recognise, plot and draw cubic, reciprocal and other given graphs, and y = sin x, cos x, tan x (3.3A, Higher).
Apply y = f(x) + a, f(ax), f(x + a) and af(x) to linear, quadratic, sine and cosine graphs (3.3B, Higher).
Interpret transformations of functions and write them algebraically (3.3C, Higher).
Find gradients of non-linear graphs by drawing a tangent (3.3D, Higher).
Use intersections of a linear and a non-linear graph to solve equations (3.3E, Higher).

units.title: Simultaneous equations
points: Solve two simultaneous linear equations exactly (2.6A).
Interpret simultaneous equations as lines meeting at the solution point (2.6B, Higher).
Solve one linear and one quadratic equation simultaneously (2.7D, Higher).

units.title: Probability
points: Use estimates and theoretical models of probability; estimate from collected data (6.3C, 6.3G).
Find probabilities from Venn diagrams and sample spaces (6.3D, 6.3E).
Use the complement and the addition rule for mutually exclusive events (6.3H, 6.3I).
Use expected frequency (6.3J).
Draw and use tree diagrams; find probabilities of independent events (6.3A, 6.3B, Higher).
Use simple conditional probability, including without replacement, and apply it to problems (6.3C, 6.3D, Higher).

units.title: Degree of accuracy
points: Identify upper and lower bounds of values given to a degree of accuracy (1.8C).
Solve problems using upper and lower bounds (1.8A, Higher).

units.title: Set language, notation and Venn diagrams
points: Understand sets, the universal set and the empty set, with their symbols (1.5A, 1.5C).
Use the notation for union, intersection, element of and complement (1.5B, 1.5D).
Represent sets with Venn diagrams (1.5E).
Understand sets defined algebraically and subsets (1.5A, Higher).
Use n(A) and Venn diagrams with numbers of elements, including practical situations (1.5B to 1.5D, Higher).

units.title: Circle properties
points: Know the parts of a circle: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector, segment (4.6).
Use the internal and external intersecting chord properties (4.6A, Higher).
Recognise a cyclic quadrilateral (4.6B, Higher).
Use circle theorems: centre and circumference, angle in a semicircle, same segment (4.6C, Higher).
Use opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral and the alternate segment theorem; formal proof not required (4.6C, Higher).

units.title: Advanced trigonometry
points: Use the sine and cosine rules for any triangle (4.8C, Higher).
Use Pythagoras' theorem in three dimensions (4.8D, Higher).
Use area = ½ab sin C (4.8E, Higher).
Solve 3D problems, including the angle between a line and a plane (4.8F, Higher).

units.title: Similar shapes
points: Understand congruence as the same shape and size (4.2F, 4.2G).
Similar figures have corresponding lengths in the same ratio and equal angles (4.11A).
Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides (4.11A, Higher).
Volumes of similar figures are in the ratio of the cubes; solve problems (4.11B, 4.11C, Higher).

units.title: Function notation
points: Understand a function as a mapping between two sets (3.2A, Higher).
Use f(x) = … and f : x ↦ … notation (3.2B, Higher).
Understand domain and range, and values excluded from a domain (3.2C, Higher).
Find composite functions fg and inverse functions f⁻¹ (3.2D, Higher).

units.title: Vectors
points: Know a vector has magnitude and direction; use vector notation, including column vectors (5.1A, 5.1B, Higher).
Multiply vectors by scalars; add and subtract vectors; find resultants (5.1C, 5.1D, 5.1F, Higher).
Calculate the modulus of a vector (5.1E, Higher).
Use vector methods for simple geometrical proofs (5.1G, Higher).

units.title: Calculus
points: Understand a variable rate of change (3.4A, Higher).
Differentiate integer powers of x (3.4B, Higher).
Find gradients, rates of change and turning points by differentiation, and relate them to graphs (3.4C, Higher).
Distinguish maxima and minima from the shape of the graph (3.4D, Higher).
Apply calculus to linear kinematics and simple practical problems (3.4E, Higher).

arabic.subject: Arabic
arabic.framework: National Curriculum in England (2013): Languages programmes of study, key stage 2 (foreign language) and key stage 3 (modern foreign language)
arabic.statusNote: The gov.uk statutory guidance page for the languages programmes of study was opened and summarised; the two programme-of-study PDFs were not separately opened. Arabic is not named in the programmes, but KS2 allows any modern or ancient foreign language and KS3 any modern foreign language. Status Provisional. November 2026 alignment with the school's own Arabic files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work (topic per half term) and the Arabic Curriculum Intent (grammar points, assessments); Years 3 to 6 keep Kitabi (pupils placed by level) with the half-term topics and grammar focus of the Tarbiyyah Primary Year 3 to 6 curriculum maps (2023-24). The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027, after induction week (4 to 8 Jan, no live lessons); Spring 1 weeks 1 and 2 (11 and 18 Jan) are a bridge of the Autumn essentials.
purpose: To give pupils an opening to other languages and cultures.
To help pupils understand and respond to spoken and written language and to communicate for practical purposes.
To speak with growing confidence, write accurately and appreciate the language's writing.
arabic.toKS4: The KS3 scheme feeds the Pearson GCSE Arabic (1AA0) themes in the order the school's GCSE scheme of work teaches them. Y8 About me, My family and Hobbies and Y9 What does he look like? feed Theme 1 Who am I? (1.1) and Cultural life (1.3); Y8 At home and Y9 Food feed Daily life (1.2); Y9 My town and Transport feed Theme 2 Town, region and country (2.3) and Travel (2.2); Y9 Clothes feeds shopping (1.2, 2.2); Y9 At school feeds Theme 3 (3.1); Y8 My job feeds Theme 4 Work (4.3). Y9 Summer 2 ends with an introduction to the GCSE course. The same grammar (agreement, plurals, tenses, imperative, participles) serves 4AA1 Paper 1 grammar.

art.subject: Art and Design
art.framework: National Curriculum in England (2013, in force from 2014): Art and design programmes of study, key stages 1 to 3; Early Years Foundation Stage (Expressive Arts and Design) for Reception
art.statusNote: Verified from official text read in full: National Curriculum art and design programmes of study (gov.uk, key stages 1 to 3, re-read October 2026); EYFS Expressive Arts and Design and Fine Motor early learning goals (statutory framework from 1 September 2026); DfE GCSE art and design subject content (January 2015). The AQA page is cited only as an example of assessment objectives. Statutory statements are by key stage; the year-by-year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory. Units marked inSchoolLessons are in the school's lesson files (two per year); other units are recommended additions with no lesson plans yet. School-choice notes, not verification gaps: the Google Drive Art scheme was not read; the GCSE board for Year 10 is not yet chosen, so no board unit references are given; Islamic art units follow the school lessons, as the National Curriculum names no artists or traditions. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the order and topics of the Tarbiyyah Secondary Art & Design Curriculum Intent (Year 7: elements of art, colour theory, still life, buildings and Hundertwasser, silhouette art, Post-Impressionism; Year 8: perspective, Islamic art, abstract art, the hand in clay, tie-dye, street art and typography; Year 9: natural forms, Fauvism, optical illusion, flower power, architecture, an abstract final composition). The Creative Arts 5-year scheme in the folder is another school's (Redstone Academy) example scheme: its still life, buildings, silhouette, optical illusion, abstract, architecture and flower topics match the intent; its portraits, human figure, wildlife, vehicles, duff lessons and outdoor trips are not adopted, nor is the intent's visiting-artist workshop. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and art and design and DT long-term plans; each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line. House rule: no drawing of people (faces or figures); subjects are objects, plants, buildings, landscapes, pattern, geometry and calligraphy (owner decision, 9 Nov 2026; the study of the hand in Year 8 is kept for now). Artists whose work shows people may be looked at; pupils do not reproduce the people.
purpose: Art, craft and design are among humanity's creative achievements and shape history and culture.
Teaching should build skill, experimentation and original work, with deeper critical thinking in older pupils.
Pupils should record ideas, master drawing, painting, sculpture and other techniques, and evaluate work using subject vocabulary.
Pupils should learn about notable artists, craft makers, designers and architects and how their fields developed.
art.toKS4: Key stage 3 prepares pupils for GCSE Art and Design, where the four assessment objectives are, in general terms: develop ideas through investigation informed by sources (AO1); refine work by experimenting with media and processes (AO2); record ideas and observations (AO3); present a personal, informed outcome (AO4). In the AQA GCSE example opened, each objective carries 25% across a portfolio (60%) and an externally set assignment (40%). Year 9 sketchbook, drawing, design and research units build those habits. The school's GCSE board and endorsement are not confirmed, so no unit references are given. The DfE GCSE subject content (January 2015, read in full) requires drawing to support development in every area of study, allows entirely digital or non-digital work, and lists seven titles: art, craft and design; fine art; graphic communication; textile design; three-dimensional design; photography; critical and contextual studies. Year 7 to 9 units on sketchbooks, drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, textiles, photography and digital work map to these titles.

computing.subject: Computing
computing.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Computing programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3), with an early-years technology foundation for Reception
computing.statusNote: Key stage statements were read and paraphrased from the gov.uk National Curriculum computing programmes of study. The EYFS statutory framework (September 2026 version) has no technology-specific early learning goal, so the Reception year map is a recommended early-skills sequence, not statutory content. Statutory content is set by key stage, not by year; the year allocation is a recommended sequence aligned to the school's existing unit names. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the order and topics of the Tarbiyyah Secondary Computing and ICT Curriculum Intent (Year 7: accounts and safety, foundations of computing, thinking like a computer, Scratch, networks and web design, cyber security, spreadsheets, a Scratch calculator; Year 8: Scratch and how computers appear smart, networks and protocols, sorting, Python; Year 9: Python, searching, databases, ethics and AI, web design). No secondary computing scheme of work was supplied, so the alignment is to the intent only; binary, logic and computer systems stay in Year 8 and 9 Spring for the International GCSE. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary computing scheme of work (2022-23; Years 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 partly filled in, Year 2 blank templates) and computing long-term plan (2023-24), which are built on the NCCE Teach Computing Curriculum (a publisher's generic scheme) with an e-awareness lesson at the start of units and named online-safety lessons. Years 3 to 6 are taught in Autumn 1, Spring 1 and Summer 1 only. Not adopted: Making Music (Year 2) and the music content of Sequencing Sounds (Year 3).
purpose: Computing education builds computational thinking and creativity, with links to mathematics, science, and design and technology.
It rests on three strands: computer science, information technology and digital literacy.
Pupils learn to write programs, solve problems by breaking them into parts, and understand how computers work.
Pupils become responsible, confident and creative users of digital technology.
computing.toKS4: Key Stage 3 prepares pupils for Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science 1CP2 (Paper 1 Topics 1 to 5, Paper 2 Topic 6 in Python 3). Algorithms, flowcharts, searching and sorting set up Topic 1 (1.1 to 1.3). Binary, data representation and file sizes set up Topic 2. Hardware, software and translators set up Topic 3. Networks and protocols set up Topic 4. Online safety, ethics, law and the environment set up Topic 5. Scratch then Python, with functions, lists and strings, set up Topic 6 (6.1 to 6.6), which is assessed by an on-screen programming exam.

english.subject: English
english.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): English programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Literacy and Communication and Language for Reception
english.statusNote: All content was compared with the official text, read as raw text from the gov.uk and assets.publishing.service.gov.uk PDFs listed in sources: the primary (KS1-2) and secondary (KS3) English programmes of study, Appendix 1 (spelling), Appendix 2 (vocabulary, grammar and punctuation), the glossary (used to check terminology) and the EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (dated 13 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026): the Communication and Language, Literacy and Fine Motor sections and Early Learning Goals. EYFS assessment and welfare sections were not needed for this syllabus. The statutory content is set by key stage (Year 1 and Year 2 individually in KS1; two-year blocks in KS2; KS3 as one block); the year-by-year allocation, the phonics order in Reception and Year 1, and the chosen texts (The Explorer, war poetry, Of Mice and Men, and similar) are the school's recommended sequence, not statutory. Spelling and grammar are recorded at topic level in paraphrase; the Year 3-4 and Year 5-6 statutory word lists are named, not reproduced. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary English schemes of work (one per Cornerstones project, the school's own adaptation of the Cornerstones English units) for texts, writing outcomes and order; projects with no school scheme among the files (Year 1 Splendid Skies, Year 4 Road Trip USA, Year 5 Scream Machine, Stargazers, Alchemy Island and Ground-Breaking Greeks, Year 6 ID) use the text types in the school's curriculum maps. Texts the school may find unsuitable are flagged TO CONFIRM, not swapped silently. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Secondary English Language and Literature Intent 2026-27 (concepts, frameworks, weekly sequence) and the 2026-27 weekly schemes of work in the Year 7, 8 and 9 half-term folders (set texts, order, weekly grammar and non-fiction, half-termly assessments). The school's HT4 Ramadan programme is taught after Ramadan (TGA has no Ramadan lessons); the 2025-26 English Literature folder (Boy in the Striped Pyjamas, Refugee Boy and others) is superseded by the 2026-27 files. The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027, with English bridge weeks on 11 and 18 Jan.
purpose: English is essential to education: pupils must speak, read and write fluently to take part in society.
Reading, especially literature, supports cultural, emotional, intellectual, social and spiritual development.
Pupils should write clearly for different audiences, and use discussion to learn and explain ideas.
Pupils build a wide vocabulary, understand grammar and conventions, and appreciate the literary heritage.
english.toKS4: KS3 prepares pupils for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language B (4EB1: one 3-hour paper with unseen reading, directed writing and a discursive, narrative or descriptive piece) and English Literature (4ET1: Component 1 unseen poetry, anthology poetry and modern prose; Component 2 modern drama and a literary heritage text). The school's KS3 texts feed these directly: Macbeth (Year 9) is the school's 4ET1 literary heritage text; Blessing (Year 8) is a 4ET1 anthology poem; conflict and identity poems (Years 7 to 9) build the comparison method (TAPS, PEMAACS) used for the anthology question; weekly non-fiction and grammar lessons build 4EB1 reading and writing.

geography.subject: Geography
geography.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Geography programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Understanding the World
geography.statusNote: Verified from official text: National Curriculum geography programmes of study for key stages 1 to 3 (gov.uk, re-read October 2026) and the EYFS Understanding the World early learning goals (People, Culture and Communities; The Natural World) in the statutory framework from 1 September 2026, read in full text. The Reception unit now follows those goals. Year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory; the National Curriculum sets content by key stage. Year units follow the school's existing unit titles. School-choice notes, not verification gaps: KS1 contrasting-country place knowledge, KS2 Europe and North America, KS3 Africa and Asia, KS3 locational knowledge, development and economic sectors, geological time, weather and climate have no matching school units yet; online pupils need a route for fieldwork (for example guided local fieldwork with a parent or tutor). Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 keep the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with each project's geography content taken from the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and geography long-term plan; fieldwork is done at home or online. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Geography Curriculum Intent (KS3 long-term overview) and the chapters of Oxford's Geog.1, Geog.2 and Geog.3 (publisher's generic schemes of work, 'oxo_' files), with Hodder's Progress in Geography KS3 units (school folder 'Pearsons'; also generic) for extra activities. Fieldwork is done at home; the intent's residential visit is not adopted. The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027.
purpose: Spark lasting curiosity about the world, its places, people and environments.
Understand the physical and human processes that shape places and how they interconnect.
Gather, analyse and communicate geographical information through maps, fieldwork, data and extended writing.
geography.toKS4: KS3 sets up Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Geography 4GE1 (Years 10 and 11). Year 7 glaciers and rivers, Year 8 coasts and Year 9 geology lead to Paper 1 river and coastal environments (Topics 1 and 2); Year 9 tectonic hazards and Year 8 tropical cyclones lead to hazardous environments (Topic 3); Year 8 climate change and Year 9 natural resources lead to fragile environments and climate change (Topic 7); Year 9 earning a living and globalisation lead to economic activity and energy (Topic 4); Year 8 urban change and population lead to urban environments (Topic 6); Year 9 development leads to Topic 9. Map, GIS and home fieldwork skills lead to the fieldwork questions in Section B of each paper.

history.subject: History
history.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): History programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Understanding the World
history.statusNote: Key Stage 1 to 3 statutory content and period lists were re-read from the gov.uk National Curriculum history programme of study (page read through a fetch tool that returns summaries, checked against the earlier reading). EYFS Understanding the World: Past and Present was read in the 13 July 2026 statutory framework (in force 1 September 2026) and the Reception row matches it. Year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory; the National Curriculum sets content by key stage. Year units follow the school's existing unit titles. History is taught from Year 1 to Year 9 only; it is not offered at Key Stage 4. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 keep the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with each project's history content taken from the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and history long-term plan (for example Year 3 Mighty Metals teaches the History of Sports Tournaments, as in the map). November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Secondary History Curriculum Intent (its KS3 programme overview sets the order and topics) and Hodder's Understanding History: Key Stage 3 scheme of work (2019; a publisher's generic scheme, in the school folder as 'Progress in History Scheme of Work KS3'), whose lesson numbers are named on each unit. The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027. History is not taught at KS4; the school's KS4 History scheme (Weimar and Nazi Germany) is not used.
purpose: Build coherent knowledge of Britain and the wider world and spark curiosity about the past.
Use evidence, interpretations and second-order concepts such as change, cause, similarity and significance.
Link local, national and international history across short and long timescales.
history.toKS4: History is not offered at Key Stage 4: the subject ends in Year 9. The KS3 skills carry into other KS4 subjects: chronology, cause and consequence and source analysis into Islamic Studies (4IS1 Section A, the life of the Prophet and the early Muslim community); context and interpretation into English Literature (4ET1 AO4, for example Jacobean England for Macbeth and 1930s America for Of Mice and Men); and change over time into Geography (development and urban change). Pupils who want GCSE History later can build on the Year 7 to Year 9 units.

islamic-studies.subject: Islamic Studies
islamic-studies.framework: Statutory RE entitlement (no National Curriculum programme of study); the school's own Islamic Studies programme
islamic-studies.statusNote: There is no National Curriculum programme of study for RE, so this is the school's own programme, taken from its lesson files (content/lessons/islamic-studies, Reception to Year 9) and the Ibn Baz course plan in the school Drive. The gov.uk RE page was opened but says nothing about independent schools. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one.
purpose: To know Allah, the Prophet and the faith of Islam through creed, worship and character.
To practise worship correctly and live by Islamic manners at home, school and online.
To build the knowledge and skills needed for the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies course.
islamic-studies.toKS4: The KS3 programme feeds the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1) sections. Section A (Prophet's life): Y7 Makkan seerah supports 1.1 to 1.4, Y8 Madinah and Badr support 1.4 and 1.8, Y9 Hudaybiyyah, Conquest and Farewell Sermon support 1.7 and 1.9, Y7 and Y9 hadith units support 1.5. Section B (beliefs): Y7 to Y9 aqidah and iman units support 2.1 to 2.6, Y8 sources of law supports 2.7, Y8 to Y9 akhlaq supports 2.8. Section C (living the Muslim life): fiqh of worship, zakah, sawm and Hajj support 3.2 to 3.5. The Ibn Baz supplementary course supports 2.1 (tawhid and shirk), 3.2 (prayer and wudu) and 2.8 (character) but does NOT cover the Prophet's life (1.1 to 1.9) or the early community (2.9). Also not yet covered: Muhammad's role in justice (1.6), Prophet as leader (1.7) in depth, the earlier prophets Musa, Dawud, Isa (2.2), jihad (3.6), festivals (3.7), marriage and family (3.8) and citizenship (3.9).

mathematics.subject: Mathematics
mathematics.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Mathematics programmes of study, with EYFS Mathematics (Number; Numerical Patterns) for Reception
mathematics.statusNote: Key stage statements were read and paraphrased from the gov.uk National Curriculum mathematics programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3) and the Reception goals from the EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (version effective September 2026). Statutory content is set by key stage, not by year. The year allocation in the year map is a recommended sequence aligned to the school's existing unit names, not a statutory requirement. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 keep the White Rose Secondary block order (block names only); each unit's resources name the matching lessons of the school's KS3 scheme, Pearson's generic KS3 Maths Progress (Second Edition), and week plans and founding-year notes follow docs/curriculum-packs/y7.md to y9.md. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and maths long-term plan and Maths policy (White Rose); each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line.
purpose: Mathematics is a creative, connected discipline used in daily life, science, engineering, finance and work.
Pupils become fluent, with quick and accurate recall of core mathematics.
Pupils reason mathematically: conjecture, generalise, justify and prove.
Pupils solve routine and unfamiliar problems by breaking them into steps and persevering.
mathematics.toKS4: Key Stage 3 prepares pupils for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1), Higher tier, taught in Years 10 and 11 in the order of Pearson's two-year 4MA1 scheme of work. Number (place value, powers, roots, standard form, fractions, percentages) sets up 4MA1 Units 1 to 8 (spec section 1); algebra, sequences and graphs set up Units 9 to 19 (sections 2 and 3); angles, constructions, area, volume, Pythagoras, similarity and transformations set up Units 20 to 29 (sections 4 and 5); averages, charts and probability set up Units 30 to 32 (section 6). Year 9 ends with quadratic graphs, tree diagrams and an introduction to trigonometry so Year 10 can begin 4MA1 at pace.

pshe.subject: PSHE
pshe.framework: Statutory guidance: Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education (revised, in force from 1 September 2026); National Curriculum in England: Citizenship programmes of study KS3 and KS4; PSHE Association programme of study (non-statutory reference); EYFS PSED for Reception. School position: PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education; puberty and bulugh taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately
pshe.statusNote: Provisional. Read in full text from official sources: the 1 September 2026 RSHE statutory guidance PDF, compared line by line with the July 2025 PDF (the two extracts are identical; the 2026 file is the July 2025 text reissued); National Curriculum citizenship KS3 and KS4 (official PDF); the EYFS PSED goals (framework from 1 September 2026); the gov.uk collection page. The DfE will not publish standalone gender-questioning guidance: it proposes to put that content in Keeping children safe in education (policy paper, 12 February 2026), so nothing separate exists to read. Not verified: the PSHE Association programme of study download (learning opportunities by key stage), which could not be opened in October 2026; its core themes (Health and wellbeing, Relationships, Living in the wider world) come from earlier reads of site pages. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. School decisions recorded (October 2026, updated 26 October): the subject is PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education (manners, friendships, families, health and hygiene, and keeping safe, including body safety at a non-sexual level and what the law says to protect young people); puberty and bulugh are taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately; parents can see all PSHE materials. Statements below quote the national guidance; the school's lessons follow these decisions. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the order and topics of the Tarbiyyah Secondary PSHE Curriculum Intent (Year 7: transition, safeguarding, wellbeing, identity and protected characteristics, growing up, first aid basics; Year 8: first aid, British values and law, respect and risk, wellbeing, helping those less fortunate, families in Britain; Year 9: marriage, family and the law, careers and options, staying safe, a community project). The PSHE folder holds the PSHE Association KS3-4 Planning Toolkit (2017), a generic planning document; only content that fits the school's rules is used (no sexuality, romance, contraception, STIs, sexting or pornography lessons). November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow Tarbiyyah Primary's PSHE scheme of work and PSHE long-term plan (the Ealing LA PSHE, Citizenship and SEAL spiral scheme, a local-authority scheme: Year A units in Years 1, 3, 5 and Year B units in Years 2, 4, 6), with every RSE and puberty lesson left out, theme weeks and festival dates not adopted, and fund-raising adapted to a sadaqah plan at home. Owner decision, 9 Nov 2026: the Year 8 and Year 9 relationships topics in the intent are taught as law and citizenship (British law, with the Islamic teaching on marriage alongside, respect for every person, no RSE content, no promotion); puberty and bulugh are taught in Year 7 only, boys and girls separately.
purpose: PSHE helps pupils stay safe and healthy and form respectful relationships, taught within an Islamic ethos.
Primary pupils (Years 1 to 6): adab, friendships, families, health, hygiene and keeping safe, including body safety. The subject is PSHE only.

Secondary pupils (Years 7 to 11): PSHE taught from an Islamic perspective, with puberty and bulugh taught in Year 7 to boys and girls separately: marriage and family, modesty, puberty and its fiqh, consent and the law, online harms and mental wellbeing.
Citizenship prepares pupils to take an active part in society, including democracy, law, rights and personal finance.
pshe.toKS4: Years 10 and 11 continue PSHE (taught from an Islamic perspective; puberty and bulugh are taught in Year 7 only, boys and girls separately) and add National Curriculum KS4 citizenship content (law, rights, democracy and personal finance). School content for Years 10 and 11 already covers stress, relationships and the law, gambling and exploitation, work, post-16 pathways, money, first aid, and consent, modesty and the law. There is no examination in this programme and no board unit references. Key stage 3 builds the vocabulary, safe-help habits and legal awareness these units extend.

quran.subject: Qur'an and Tajweed
quran.statusNote: No National Curriculum or exam-board framework exists for Qur'an and Tajweed. This is the school's own programme, drawn from its lesson files (Reception to Year 9) and the tajweed-by-year layout of the old Drive Quran tracker. Recitation follows the Madinah mushaf, Hafs 'an 'Asim. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one.
purpose: To read the Qur'an fluently and accurately from the mushaf with correct tajweed.
To memorise selected surahs securely and keep them through revision.
To understand the meaning of what is recited and to show adab with the Qur'an.
Standard: Arabic script is always shown with transliteration, never transliteration alone.
quran.toKS4: There is no Qur'an qualification at KS4 in this pack. Year 10 and 11 lesson files continue the programme (Ayat al-Kursi 2:255, Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4, Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-10) and support Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1), whose set passages (for example 97:1-5, 112:1-4, 2:183-185) are studied in Arabic and English. Qur'an lessons give recitation and meaning for these passages in sections 1.2, 2.1 and 3.3.

science.subject: Science
science.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Science programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3); Reception aligned to EYFS Understanding the World: The Natural World
science.statusNote: Key Stage 1, 2 and 3 statements were read from the gov.uk National Curriculum science programme of study; the whole page, including the end of the Key Stage 4 section, has now been read, and a sample of Year 2 to Year 6 statements was re-checked against the official primary PDF with no errors found. EYFS Understanding the World: The Natural World was read in the 13 July 2026 statutory framework (in force 1 September 2026) and the Reception row is consistent with it. Statutory content is set by key stage and by named year for KS1 and KS2; the Year 7 to Year 9 allocation and all unit titles are a recommended sequence because the National Curriculum sets Key Stage 3 content as a whole. Pages were read through a fetch tool that summarises text. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow Pearson Exploring Science units in the order of the Tarbiyyah Secondary Biology, Chemistry and Physics curriculum intents (two units a half term); resources name Exploring Science and Kerboodle Activate for AQA, both generic publisher schemes held by the school. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and science long-term plan; each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line.
purpose: Science builds understanding of the world through biology, chemistry and physics, with core knowledge, methods and uses.
Pupils develop key concepts that spark curiosity and help them explain, predict and analyse causes.
Pupils learn how scientific enquiry works so they can judge science's uses and implications now and later.
Precise technical vocabulary is expected, and schools may teach content earlier or later within a key stage.
science.toKS4: KS3 sets up Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science (Double Award) 4SD0. Cells, organ systems, food, breathing, respiration and plants (7A, 7C, 8A, 8C, 9B) lead to Biology 1 and 2; reproduction, variation and genetics (8B, 7B, 9A) lead to Biology 3; ecosystems, decomposers and sampling (7D, 8D, 9D) lead to Biology 4 and 5. Particles, separation, acids, atoms, the periodic table and metals (7E to 7H, 8F, 8G) lead to Chemistry 1 and 2; combustion, energy in reactions and materials (8E, 9E, 9F) lead to Chemistry 3 and 4. Forces, electricity, sound and light, fluids and energy (7I to 7L, 8I to 8K, 9I, 9J) lead to Physics 1 to 6; Earth and space (8L) leads to Physics 8. Working scientifically (9C) feeds the practical skills examined in all three papers.
